advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Use `urllib.request.proxy_bypass_environment(host, self._proxies)` in `_transport_for` so NO_PROXY comes from the same snapshot taken at build time
evidence: src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py:174: restores that behaviour. The variables are read once, here, through the standard library's
src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py:181:     proxies = urllib.request.getproxies_environment()
src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py:225:         if urllib.request.proxy_bypass(host):
stdlib proxy_bypass() (and proxy_bypass_environment with proxies=None) calls getproxies_environment() on each call, so the saved self._proxies is not used for the NO_PROXY decision
advisory.finding: The docstring says the proxy variables are read once, when the transport is built. That holds for HTTP(S)_PROXY and ALL_PROXY. NO_PROXY does not follow it: `_transport_for` calls `urllib.request.proxy_bypass(host)` on every request, and that call reads `getproxies_environment()` again each time instead of using the saved `self._proxies['no']`. A change to NO_PROXY after the client is built would then be applied using proxies captured earlier, and os.environ is scanned on every request.
scenarios: NO_PROXY is set or changed in-process after the LLM client is built: the bypass decision uses the new NO_PROXY while proxy selection still uses the values captured at build time
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace `urllib.request.proxy_bypass(host)` with `urllib.request.proxy_bypass_environment(host, self._proxies)`. This uses the stored snapshot, matches the 'read once' docstring, and avoids the platform-dependent proxy_bypass dispatch.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make test_httpx2_transport_routes_through_proxy call _build_httpx2_tenacity_transport without `wrapped=` so the edited fallback lines run
evidence: tests/unit/test_llm_env_proxy.py:199-203: `transport = _build_httpx2_tenacity_transport(httpx2, config={"reraise": True}, wrapped=_env_proxy_aware_transport(httpx2),)`
src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py:125: `wrapped=wrapped or _env_proxy_aware_transport(httpx2),`
src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py:132: `self.wrapped = wrapped or _env_proxy_aware_transport(httpx2)`
tests/unit/test_llm_env_proxy.py:187 docstring claims: "The httpx2 branch gets the same proxy-aware transport inside its retry wrapper."
Named call: `_build_httpx2_tenacity_transport(httpx2, config={...}, wrapped=None)` with HTTPS_PROXY set is never made, so no test reaches lines 125/132.
advisory.finding: test_httpx2_transport_routes_through_proxy builds the wrapped transport itself (`wrapped=_env_proxy_aware_transport(httpx2)`), so the edited `wrapped or _env_proxy_aware_transport(httpx2)` fallback lines in _build_httpx2_tenacity_transport never run. The test redoes the wiring instead of driving it. If either line went back to `httpx2.AsyncHTTPTransport()`, the test would still pass.
scenarios: Someone reverts line 125 or 132 to `httpx2.AsyncHTTPTransport()`: test_httpx2_transport_routes_through_proxy stays green, yet a caller that passes no wrapped transport loses proxy routing.
advisory.suggested_fix: Drop `wrapped=_env_proxy_aware_transport(httpx2)` from the call at tests/unit/test_llm_env_proxy.py:199-203 (pass `wrapped=None`), so the default `wrapped or _env_proxy_aware_transport(httpx2)` path builds the routing transport under the patched recorder.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test showing http_client.aclose() closes both the direct transport and every proxy transport
evidence: src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py:241-243: `async def aclose(self) -> None: for transport in (self._direct, *self._via.values()): await transport.aclose()`
tests/unit/test_llm_env_proxy.py:62-66: the recorder's transport is `self._http.MockTransport(_handler)` and records only `handled`, never close/enter/exit

Named sequence: set HTTPS_PROXY=http://proxy.example:3128, build the provider client, send one request, `await http_client.aclose()`. Nothing asserts that the transport built with `proxy=` was closed.
src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py:255: `return value if "://" in value else f"http://{value}"`
tests/unit/test_llm_env_proxy.py:28-29: `_PROXY = "http://proxy.example:3128"`, `_OTHER_PROXY = "http://all-proxy.example:8080"`. Both include a scheme.
Named input: HTTPS_PROXY="proxy.example:3128" should route via a transport built with proxy="http://proxy.example:3128"; no test sets it.
advisory.finding: _EnvProxyRoutingTransport's new aclose/__aenter__/__aexit__ must reach the proxy transports in `_via` as well as `_direct`, but no test checks this. The _Recorder returns plain MockTransports that record no close calls, so a regression that closes only `_direct` would go unnoticed.
merged_from: The bare host:port normalization in _proxy_url (`value if "://" in value else f"http://{value}"`) is new and never tested. Every test proxy value includes a scheme.
scenarios: A refactor closes only self._direct: proxy connection pools leak on every gate run, and every test still passes.
advisory.suggested_fix: Have the _Recorder return a MockTransport subclass that records aclose() along with its proxy label. After the client's aclose(), assert the closed labels equal {None, _PROXY}.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add httpx.ProxyError (via http_module.ProxyError) to the transport retry rule in _build_retrying_anthropic_provider, and classify it in failure._map, so transient proxy CONNECT failures keep the retry and backoff that direct ConnectError gets.
evidence: Primary failure: the upstream LLM endpoint is briefly unreachable or overloaded. Over a direct connection this surfaces as httpx.ConnectError (a NetworkError).

Secondary path added by this change: src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py:227 `return self._via[proxy]` sends the request through AsyncHTTPTransport(proxy=url) (src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py:203). There, a non-2xx CONNECT response from the proxy raises httpx.ProxyError instead (resolve_symbol shows httpx.ProxyError exists; in httpx it is a TransportError, not a NetworkError).
Retry rule that changes behaviour: src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py:363-365 retries only `HTTPStatusError | TimeoutException | NetworkError`, so ProxyError is not retried.
SDK retries are disabled: src/rebar/llm/anthropic_model.py:390 `max_retries=0`, and docstring line 326 says 'The transport alone owns retries'. Nothing else retries the request.
Before: a direct transient connect failure surfaced as ConnectError, was retried with backoff by the transport, and classify_llm_failure maps it to RETRY_NOW (src/rebar/llm/failure.py:285-286).

After: a transient proxy CONNECT failure surfaces as httpx.ProxyError after a single attempt. failure.py has no ProxyError branch (searching src/rebar for 'ProxyError' finds nothing). A raw ProxyError would fall through to NEEDS_INVESTIGATION (src/rebar/llm/failure.py:310). If the SDK or pydantic-ai wrap it first as a connection error, it is still classified retryable, but the transport-level backoff has already been skipped.
advisory.finding: HTTPS requests now go through a proxy tunnel (CONNECT). When the proxy refuses or fails that tunnel (for example 502, 503 or 504 because the proxy is overloaded or cannot reach the upstream), httpx raises httpx.ProxyError. That is a TransportError, not a NetworkError or TimeoutException, so the retry wrapper surfaces it after one attempt with no backoff. The direct-connection failures it stands in for (ConnectError, which is a NetworkError) were retried up to llm_retry_max_attempts times.
scenarios: A host whose only egress is a corporate or sandbox proxy (the case this change targets). The proxy briefly returns 503 to CONNECT api.anthropic.com, and the gate call fails at once instead of backing off and retrying.
advisory.suggested_fix: In _build_retrying_anthropic_provider, add `| retry_if_exception_type(http_module.ProxyError)` to the RetryConfig retry rule. In failure._map, map `httpx.ProxyError` to RETRY_NOW next to the ConnectError branch.

docs/generated-artifacts.md:14: docs/env-vars.md is generated from an AST scan of env reads. The urllib-based read is not one of the patterns it recognizes (docs/env-vars.md:7-11), so the generated registry will not list these variables either.
advisory.finding: LLM calls now follow the standard proxy environment variables with rebar-specific rules, but the maintained LLM configuration env-var table in `docs/llm-framework.md` does not mention them. The rules: loopback hosts always go direct, the macOS/Windows system proxy settings are not used, and unusable values are skipped with a warning. An operator on a host that can only reach the internet through a proxy cannot learn from the table that these variables are honoured, or how loopback and system-proxy handling differs from httpx defaults.
scenarios: An operator on a host that can only reach the internet through a proxy sets HTTPS_PROXY and expects a loopback OpenAI-compatible endpoint to go through the proxy, but rebar always sends loopback requests direct.
A macOS user relies on system proxy settings, as other httpx-based tools do, and gate calls still fail because rebar reads only environment variables.
advisory.suggested_fix: In docs/llm-framework.md, add a row next to the `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` row (line 440). Example: `HTTPS_PROXY` / `HTTP_PROXY` / `ALL_PROXY` / `NO_PROXY` | unset | standard proxy variables honoured by the Anthropic and OpenAI-compatible LLM clients, chosen per request URL (scheme proxy, else `ALL_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY` hosts direct). Loopback hosts always connect directly. The macOS/Windows system proxy settings are not used. A value no transport can use is skipped with a warning.
